title: Object Constructor
body:
```js
const car = new Object();
// or
const car = {};
```

One of the three ways to make an object, per [[Objects]]. `new Object()` and `{}` produce the
same thing, and the literal form is what everyone actually writes; see [[Object Literal]].

```js
const car = new Object();
car.make = "Mazda";       // properties are added by assigning them

const car2 = { make: "Mazda" };   // same object, one line
```

Objects in JS are open: assigning to a property that does not exist creates it, and there is
no class declaration listing what a car is allowed to have. That is the flexibility, and it is
also why a typo'd property name is a silent bug rather than a
[[Compile Errors|compile error]] the way it would be in C++.

The third way, [[Constructor Functions]], is the one to reach for when you need many objects
with the same shape.
